item.title: Evals: Four Numbers That Tell You Whether an AI System Actually Works
item.description: 中文版是这篇文章的默认版本。 阅读中文版 → This English page stays available at this URL; the Chinese version is the one we maintain first. An eval spends most of its budget on reading outputs and labelling cases. Code is the cheap part. This piece splits the work into four parts and gives each part a number you can recompute. The film runs one minute forty-four, voiced in English, with the captions burned in and switchable in the player.

item.title: Seven layers between the model and the result: reading the guide against its own evidence
item.description: 中文版是这篇文章的默认版本。 阅读中文版 → This English page stays available at this URL; the Chinese version is the one we maintain first. Abstract. Most production agent failures do not happen in the model layer. Split the distance from model to result into seven layers — model, instructions and context, tools, memory, loop, evals and guardrails, human signature — and the most common reflex (swap the model, rewrite the prompt) acts on the one layer least likely to be broken.
